asha: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak to prefer the new fused-attn kernel, TP runs with 8 GPUs show a 12-18% end-to-end latency regression for long-context (>4k) prompts.

ben: ugh. is it across all models or just the big ones?

asha: Mostly the 7B-30B family; 70B looks unaffected. Regression correlates with higher frequency of small all-reduce packets during KV flushes. Profiling snapshot attached below.

maria: can you paste the perf trace? nvprof / nsight sample will help.

asha: pasted quick perf snippet:
```
# from perf-agent: tp_step=0x7f1a, timeline (ms):
compute_start 0.0
compute_end 12.6
allreduce_start 12.7 (12x 2KB msgs)
allreduce_end 25.4
compute_start 25.6
...
```
Small-ish allreduce windows (~2KB msgs) happening 12x per step, causing NCCL to favor ring with many hops.

raj: interesting — ring is better for large msgs but suffers on many tiny collective ops. tree (or tree+scatter) can reduce hop count for small messages. what does `NCCL_COLL_NET` show?

ben: also double-check kernel selection changed sequence lengths/tiling which might increase KV eviction frequency and thus more KV-chunk flushes. could be batching heuristic interacting badly.

asha: perf-bot produced flame/trace link: https://perf.redwood/test/24278?view=timeline (internal)

maria: quick repro idea: run microbenchmark that simulates KV cache flush pattern: burst of 12x2KB allreduces interleaved with 10ms compute. measure ring vs tree. I'll spin it up.

raj: try toggling NCCL_ALGO and NCCL_THRESHOLD too. Also test NCCL_TREE for reductions. I suspect the kernel change reduces compute saturation so comm becomes dominant and we didn't update chunking heuristics.

ben: agree. If compute shortens, interleaving gets noisier. Two experiments: (1) increase chunk size (coalesce adjacent KV fragments) to reduce number of allreduces, (2) force tree algorithm to see latency delta.

asha: added experiment matrix to runbook: coalesce_bytes = [2KB, 8KB, 32KB], NCCL_ALGO=[RING,TREE], warmup runs=200, measure p99 and tokens/sec.

maria: ran first pass (8GPU, 30B model) — preliminary numbers: 2KB baseline p99=220ms, 8KB p99=185ms, 32KB p99=178ms. TREE on 2KB gave 196ms. So coalescing looks most effective.

ben: nice. does coalescing change memory pressure / KV cache hit rates?

maria: slight uptick in transient memory but within limits; KV hit-rate unchanged. The tradeoff is extra latency for some single-token requests due to waiting to coalesce, but for batched workloads the end-to-end SLO improves.

raj: we should add adaptive coalescing: when compute time drops below threshold, enlarge coalesce window; otherwise keep minimal. Could be a runtime heuristic: target allreduce_count_per_step <= 4.

asha: agreed. I'll prototype heuristic + a guardrail flag `tp.coalesce.adaptive=true` and run canary on dedicated infra.

ben: also file a follow-up task to update kernel-selection tests to include comm/compute overlap scenarios (short compute windows) so we don't regress this again.

asha: created task INF-4217 and assigned to me. Can folks +1 the plan?

raj: +1

maria: +1, and I'll push the microbenchmark code to perf repo after tidy up.

perf-bot: snapshot saved: perf://snapshots/2427801234/ (sha: b4c12f) :white_check_mark:

asha: thanks all — next steps: run adaptive coalesce canary, compare p50/p95/p99 and cost impact, then roll if stable. I'll update thread with numbers. :rocket:
